harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as an inter-VLAN router between node2 and node3. node1's eth1 was assigned 192.168.11.1/24 facing node2 (192.168.11.2/24) and eth2 was assigned 192.168.12.1/24 facing node3 (192.168.12.2/24), with IPv4 forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. Static routes were added on node2 (to 192.168.12.0/24 via node1) and node3 (to 192.168.11.0/24 via node1). Verified node2 and node3 can ping each other across the VLAN boundary with TTL=63, proving traffic is routed through node1. All configuration was persisted (SONiC via /etc/network/interfaces.d and /etc/sysctl.d; Alpine via /etc/network/interfaces with an `up ip route` hook). Then ran the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot_id, interface/route state, ping tests) on all three nodes, restarted node2, node3, and node1 sequentially (one at a time), polled each until it came back, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified persisted routing config and end-to-end cross-VLAN ping after every restart, including after node1 (the router) came back last.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 interfaces, routes, and OS to map topology (SONiC on node1, Alpine on node2/node3)
Performed SONiC pre-config cleanup on node1 (stripped docker0 class-E IP, stopped interfaces-config.service)
Assigned 192.168.11.1/24 to node1 eth1 and 192.168.12.1/24 to node1 eth2
Assigned 192.168.11.2/24 to node2 eth1 and 192.168.12.2/24 to node3 eth1; confirmed correct wiring via ping
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1
Added static routes on node2 and node3 via node1 for the opposite subnet
Verified end-to-end cross-VLAN ping (TTL=63) between node2 and node3
Persisted config: /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-vlan-routing and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf on node1; appended eth1 stanzas with route hooks to /etc/network/interfaces on node2 and node3
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, addresses, routes, forwarding sysctls) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and full recovery of IP/route/connectivity
Restarted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and full recovery of IP/route/connectivity
Restarted node1 (router) last, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and full recovery of IP/forwarding config
Re-verified node2<->node3 cross-VLAN ping after all three restarts completed

evidence.requirement: node1 has a routed interface inside each VLAN with IPs assigned
node1 forwards traffic between the two VLANs (IP forwarding enabled)
evidence.summary: net.ipv4.ip_forward, conf.eth1.forwarding, conf.eth2.forwarding all set to 1

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other across the VLAN boundary via node1
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ping between 192.168.11.2 and 192.168.12.2 succeeds with TTL=63, proving a routed hop through node1

evidence.requirement: Configuration persists across reboot (routing survives restart)
evidence.summary: Persistent config files written: node1 /etc/network/interfaces.d + /etc/sysctl.d; node2/node3 /etc/network/interfaces with static eth1 + route hook

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b3046825...; reboot ack via dropped exec stream; post-restart boot_id 23976405... (changed); recovered eth1 IP, routes, and successful cross-VLAN ping

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 94029864...; reboot ack via dropped exec stream; post-restart boot_id 806f01f3... (changed); recovered eth1 IP, routes, and successful cross-VLAN ping

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e5a08f0f...; reboot acked; post-restart boot_id 2daee871... (changed); recovered eth1/eth2 IPs and forwarding sysctls, and re-verified node2<->node3 cross-VLAN ping after all three nodes were restarted
